title: Accuracy of an automated urgent-message flag for patient portal messages in primary care: a multi-clinic diagnostic accuracy study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the sensitivity and specificity of a vendor's urgent-message flag for patient portal messages. Design: diagnostic accuracy study with the flag in silent mode against an adjudicated two-clinician reference standard, in clinics A and B after clinic C paused. Results will follow sampling.
introduction: Portal message volume drives clinician after-hours work; automated triage could help, but accuracy varies by population and language.
methods: Random weekly samples; two blinded clinician raters with adjudication; sensitivity and specificity with Wilson intervals, by clinic and subgroup.
results: No data have been collected yet.
discussion: The discussion will weigh accuracy against the workload problem and state what is not known for messages in other languages.
limitations: Two clinics after clinic C paused; imperfect reference standard; one flag version.
summary: STARD report structure with results left empty.
